name: AWS QuickSight
headline: AWS-Native Business Intelligence (Amazon Quick Suite)
overview:
Amazon QuickSight is AWS’s serverless, cloud-native business intelligence service — now evolving into Amazon Quick Suite (October 2025) — for dashboards, pixel-perfect reports, embedded analytics, ML insights (anomaly detection, forecasting), and Amazon Q generative BI (natural-language Q&A, executive summaries, data stories). Its SPICE in-memory engine scales to billions of rows and it plugs natively into the AWS data stack (Redshift, Athena, S3, RDS, Glue). It is a general-purpose BI and visualization layer, not a marketing decision-intelligence platform: no marketing-data connector library, no ETL/TEMS, no marketing science or attribution models — and it assumes you build and manage your own AWS data plumbing, with usage/capacity/SPICE/Q pricing that is complex to estimate.

Data They Access: Native AWS data services (Redshift, Athena, S3, RDS, Aurora, Glue, OpenSearch, Timestream) plus third-party connectors (Snowflake, Databricks, Postgres, SQL Server, Oracle, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Adobe Analytics) via direct query, SPICE import, or API. No dedicated marketing-connector library across ad platforms.

Who They Target: AWS-centered data and BI teams that want serverless dashboards and embedded analytics close to Redshift/Athena/S3, and have the AWS skills to build and manage the underlying data plumbing.
insight: "Reframe: QuickSight gives AWS-native teams cheap, serverless dashboards — but you still build the data plumbing yourself, and it has no data connectors, ETL, science, or attribution. MADTECH.AI is the all-inclusive, all-industry decision-intelligence platform — connectors, warehouse, 600+ models, and MADi — with no AWS engineering required."

Flat-rate, tiered by suite, module, and solution
Structure

Reader $3/mo · Reader Pro $20 · Author $24 · Author Pro $40; Standard edition $9/user/mo (annual). Enterprise required for SSO, row-level security, embedding, alerts, and Amazon Q. Capacity/session pricing for embedded or bursty use.
Transparent, value-based, all-inclusive. No per-record, per-connector, or destination fees.
Public Pricing

Per-role pricing is published (aws.amazon.com/quicksight/pricing), but true cost adds SPICE capacity, Amazon Q question capacity, the $250/mo Q fee, embedded sessions, and Redshift/Athena/Glue compute — hard to estimate up front.
15-day free trial. iPaaS $999/mo · Decision Intelligence Growth $1,999/mo · Decision Intelligence Suite $2,999/mo (billed annually).

High — fixed costs, no surprises. Connectors, warehouse, dashboards & 24/7 support included.

Reviewers note limited visual customization, tricky security/permissions, and the need for AWS knowledge — QuickSight is easiest for AWS-native data teams, not self-serve marketers.

name: Accurate Append
headline: Data Append & Enrichment Services
overview:
Accurate Append is a data-append and enrichment vendor: you submit a list (names, postal addresses) via batch file or API and it returns missing fields — phone numbers, email addresses, and household demographics. It is a focused enrichment service with strong phone coverage and same-day turnaround, but it is a single-purpose data utility — not an analytics, warehousing, or decision-intelligence platform. Pricing is per-match with custom quotes and minimums, and email match rates can be uneven.

Data They Access: Customer/prospect lists submitted by the client (names, addresses) matched against consumer data files.

Who They Target: Call-center, direct-mail, and outreach teams needing phone/email/demographic enrichment on lists.
insight: "Accurate Append fills in missing contact fields; MADTECH.AI cleans, enriches, unifies, warehouses, and models your data — enrichment is one built-in step, not a separate per-match invoice."

name: Adverity
headline: Enterprise Marketing Data & ETL Platform
overview:
Adverity is an enterprise marketing data platform built on 600+ connectors with automated ETL/ELT, advanced transformations, data governance, and built-in agentic/conversational AI (Data Conversations). Founded in 2015 in Vienna, it serves Fortune 500 brands and agencies (Unilever, Bosch, IKEA, GroupM, Publicis, Dentsu). It splits into Adverity Data and Adverity Intelligence, requires a bring-your-own warehouse and a BI tool for visualization, and prices by quote with a 30–60 day onboarding.

Data They Access: 600+ connectors across advertising, social, e-commerce, CRM, sales and finance (Google/Meta/Amazon Ads, LinkedIn, Shopify, Salesforce) plus Webhook/Mailgun/file ingestion; destinations to bring-your-own warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift) and BI tools (Tableau, Power BI, Looker).

Who They Target: Mid-market to enterprise brands and agencies with in-house data-engineering resources that need flexible, high-volume marketing ETL, governance, and multi-brand reporting at scale.
insight: "Reframe: Adverity centralizes and cleans your marketing data brilliantly, but you still need data engineers, a separate warehouse, and a BI tool to answer why performance moved — MADTECH.AI turns that same data into no-code decision intelligence."

name: CharityEngine

name: Dexibit
headline: Visitor Attraction Analytics (now Accesso Intelligence)

name: DonorPerfect
headline: Veteran Fundraising CRM for Nonprofits
overview:
DonorPerfect is a long-established fundraising CRM from SofterWare, Inc., founded in 1987 and serving nearly 11,000 nonprofit organizations across arts, healthcare, education, and faith-based sectors. Its deep maturity shows in robust reporting, extensive training resources, and consistently praised customer support (96% positive per SelectHub aggregation). Who They Target: Small to large nonprofits wanting an established, deep fundraising CRM with strong onboarding, training, and support over a modern interface.

name: Fonteva
headline: Association Management on Salesforce
overview:
Fonteva is a Salesforce-native association management system (AMS) for membership, events, and communities, with configurable dashboards and deep Salesforce embedding. It is an operational AMS, not a marketing intelligence platform — no ETL product, no independent warehouse, no marketing science, no attribution — with months-long Salesforce implementations, customization complexity as the top complaint, and AI only via Einstein/Agentforce.

Geckoboard is purposely designed to display metrics — it cannot blend data from different datasets, run calculations, or provide any analytical depth. Verified user reviews confirm there is no way to drill into data, compare metrics across sources, or identify root causes of performance changes.

2  Per-Dashboard Cost Spikes
Geckoboard's Essential plan includes only one dashboard; additional dashboards cost $25/month each as add-ons. A Capterra reviewer noted switching from $59/month (legacy) to $149/month suddenly for fewer dashboards. Teams needing scale face disproportionate costs.

Geckoboard has zero attribution modeling capability. Marketing teams can display spend and conversion numbers side-by-side but cannot determine which channels, campaigns, or touchpoints actually drove results — making budget optimization impossible from within the platform.

Geckoboard offers no white-label capability, custom domain removal, or embedded analytics on any plan — confirmed on geckoboard.com/pricing. Agencies and media companies cannot deliver branded dashboards to clients using Geckoboard.

name: Power BI

Microsoft Power BI is a general-purpose, self-service business-intelligence and visualization tool. It is powerful and flexible, but marketing teams must build everything themselves: it ships no pre-built data connectors (third-party tools like Supermetrics are required), no included data warehouse (Fabric capacity is a separate cost), and no marketing science such as MMM or attribution. Data They Access: Any data via general connectors and Power Query; marketing sources require third-party connectors (e.g. Supermetrics).

Who They Target: All industries and roles — analysts, data teams, and enterprises standardized on Microsoft/Azure.

Salesforce Marketing Intelligence (formerly Datorama) is an enterprise marketing analytics product within Marketing Cloud, offering data pipelines, a semantic model, Tableau Next dashboards, multi-touch attribution, and Agentforce AI. Its full power — Total Connect, Agentforce, conversational AI — requires separately licensed Salesforce Data Cloud, with complex implementation, premium-priced 24/7 support, and no white-label.

Data They Access: Paid-media and Salesforce-ecosystem data natively; third-party sources via Data Pipelines / Total Connect (which require Salesforce Data Cloud). Semantic model via Tableau Semantics.

Who They Target: Enterprise marketing organizations — typically existing Salesforce/Marketing Cloud customers — with budget for a full ecosystem and implementation resources.
insight: Salesforce Marketing Intelligence is powerful — but its best features require separately licensed Data Cloud, implementation is complex and consultant-heavy, 24/7 support costs ~30% more, and there’s no marketing-science library or white-label. MADTECH.AI delivers unified intelligence self-serve, warehouse and 24/7 support included, at flat-rate pricing.

name: Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud
headline: Nonprofit CRM (now Agentforce Nonprofit)
overview:
Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud — renamed Agentforce Nonprofit in October 2025 — is Salesforce’s purpose-built nonprofit CRM, the successor to the free, community-built Nonprofit Success Pack (NPSP), whose feature development ended in March 2023. Built on the Salesforce platform and used across 56,000+ nonprofit organizations, it unifies donor/constituent management, fundraising, grantmaking, program and volunteer management, and case management, with Agentforce/Einstein AI and the full AppExchange ecosystem. It is a powerful, highly customizable system of record — but its value depends on consultants and a dedicated admin, its best data and AI features require separately licensed Data Cloud, and it has no native marketing attribution or decision-science layer.

Data They Access: The Salesforce platform and AppExchange ecosystem (MuleSoft, Data Cloud, Marketing Cloud, thousands of apps) via APIs; unifying external marketing and ad data requires separately licensed Data Cloud or middleware. No native marketing-data connector library across ad platforms and web analytics.

Who They Target: Mid-size to large nonprofits, foundations, and NGOs with the budget and admin/consultant resources to implement and maintain an enterprise CRM — and to migrate off NPSP.
insight: "Reframe: Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud is a powerful donor system of record, but unifying your marketing, ad, and program data and proving channel ROI means buying Data Cloud and hiring consultants — MADTECH.AI is the no-code decision-intelligence layer that sits on top and answers why performance moved."

name: Sidekick Solutions LLC

Who They Target: Small-to-mid nonprofits needing CRM implementation, data migration, database cleanup, and Zapier-based automation across their existing tools.
insight: Sidekick is a nonprofit-tech consultancy, not a platform — it configures and cleans up other people’s tools via Zapier, with no self-serve warehouse, dashboards, science, or AI. name: The Digital Co-Op
headline: Cooperative Donor Acquisition Data Pool (MissionWired)
overview:
The Digital Co-Op is a cooperative donor-acquisition data pool operated by the agency MissionWired, with 330+ member nonprofits sharing anonymized donor and behavioral data points. Machine-learning models identify new-to-you email, SMS, and lapsed-donor prospects on a fixed-cost basis. It is a single-purpose acquisition tool, not a marketing or fundraising decision intelligence platform — there is no dashboard, data warehouse, attribution modeling, or self-serve analytics; results are delivered via the MissionWired team.

Data They Access: Shared cooperative data lake of 150M+ email addresses pooled from 330+ member nonprofits, built on Databricks.

Who They Target: Nonprofits and political campaigns running direct-response digital fundraising programs, especially those in the progressive/advocacy space.
insight: The Co-Op grows your list one channel at a time through an agency; MADTECH.AI unifies every channel you already have into one decision intelligence hub you control.

challenges:
1  No Self-Serve Visibility
The Digital Co-Op delivers acquisition lists through an agency relationship with no dashboard, no warehouse, and no way for the nonprofit to query its own performance data directly. Every insight comes through MissionWired's reporting cadence.

2  Single-Channel, Single-Purpose Tool
The Co-Op only solves one problem: finding new-to-you donor and SMS prospects. It does not unify CRM, ticketing, fundraising, and marketing data, and offers no attribution or marketing-effectiveness measurement.

3  Opaque, Contract-Based Pricing
There is no public pricing page; nonprofits must enter a sales conversation and sign an agreement before learning what membership costs or how renewal pricing works.

4  Dependent on a Third-Party Data Pool
The Co-Op's value depends entirely on the size and quality of its shared 330-member data lake. If member composition shifts, or a nonprofit's mission does not align well with the pool's donor base, lookalike quality can vary unpredictably.

name: integrate.io
headline: Low-Code ETL & Data Pipeline Platform
overview:
integrate.io (formerly Xplenty) is a low-code ETL/ELT and reverse-ETL platform with a visual drag-and-drop pipeline builder used to move and transform data between sources, warehouses, CRMs, and ERPs. It is a data-movement layer only — it provides no included warehouse, no analytics or BI, no marketing science models, and no AI decision intelligence.

Data They Access: Databases, SaaS apps, and files piped to warehouses/CRMs (Salesforce, NetSuite, HubSpot) via low-code ETL/ELT and reverse ETL.

Who They Target: Data engineers and RevOps teams needing operational ETL without heavy code.
insight: "integrate.io builds the pipes; it does not build the answers — MADTECH.AI moves the same data and then delivers the warehouse, dashboards, models, and prescriptive AI it stops short of."
